method_note: Chose claims by risk to a test oracle: ETSI NGSI-LD mechanisms and clause numbers (checked against the V1.9.1 PDF text extracted locally), W3C WoT media types and endpoints, DTDL context strings, repository metadata (gh api), OPC 30450-1 listing facts, press-release dates, all 20 literature DOIs (Crossref), IDS approval date, and every existing_check mapping against docs/reference/capabilities.md. ESPR article numbers could not be re-read because EUR-Lex returned empty text in this session (three attempts).

checked.claim: ETSI GS CIM 009 is at V1.9.1, dated 2025-07, a group specification.
checked.evidence: Title page reads ETSI GS CIM 009 V1.9.1 (2025-07), GROUP SPECIFICATION, produced by the CIM ISG with a disclaimer that it does not represent all ETSI members.

checked.claim: Context is supplied in a Link header with rel http://www.w3.org/ns/json-ld#context.
checked.evidence: Spec examples show a Link header with that exact rel value.

checked.claim: Entity creation answers 201 with a Location header.
checked.evidence: The create-entity operation table lists 201 Created and states the response includes a Location header. The error type AlreadyExists exists in the spec; a duplicate create is an error case, which supports the failure mode about a duplicate id.

checked.claim: GeoJSON responses use application/geo+json and pagination uses a Link header with rel next.
checked.evidence: Spec text names application/geo+json in the Accept handling and shows a Link header with rel="next" in a pagination example.

checked.claim: Resources exist at /ngsi-ld/v1/entities, /temporal/entities, /types, /attributes.
checked.evidence: Clause 6 lists Resource: entities/, entities/{entityId}, temporal/entities/, temporal/entities/{entityId}, types/, types/{type}, attributes/, attributes/{attrId}. The /ngsi-ld/v1 prefix appears in the examples.

checked.claim: Clause 4.3.6.8 holds conformance fallbacks for Property and Relationship.
checked.evidence: The clause exists, but its title is 'Backwards compatibility of Context Source payloads'. Its tables cover Entity, Property and Relationship fallbacks by spec version.
checked.correction: Cite 4.3.6.8 by its title (backwards compatibility of Context Source payloads), not as 'conformance fallbacks for Property and Relationship'.

checked.claim: Clause numbers 5.2.22 KeyValuePair, 5.6.9 Batch Update, 5.6.20 Batch Merge, 5.7 Consumption, 5.8 Subscription, 5.9 Context Source Registration, EntityMap in 5.2.
checked.evidence: Table of contents: 5.2.22 KeyValuePair, 5.2.39 EntityMap, 5.6.7 Batch Entity Creation, 5.6.9 Batch Entity Update, 5.6.20 Batch Entity Merge, 5.7 Context Information Consumption, 5.8 Context Information Subscription, 5.9 Context Source Registration. Clause 5.15 is 'Context Source Identity Information', so the range '5.9 to 5.15' also covers a non-registration clause.
checked.correction: In L09, say 'clauses 5.9 onward' or '5.9 to 5.14 plus identity information in 5.15'; minor.

checked.claim: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 Art. 2(30) unique identifier enabling web link; 10(1)(b) carriers; 10(1)(d) open interoperable network; 10(4) back-up copy; 11(b) access by actor class; 11(g); 13 registry; 2(32); 2(46); 9(1); 11(d).
checked.evidence: Three EUR-Lex fetches returned empty text. A search found only secondary pages, which say Art. 10 covers DPP requirements, the back-up copy sits in Art. 10(4), and unique identifiers have their own Article 12. The file never cites Art. 12, which a secondary source associates with unique identifiers.
checked.correction: Re-verify every article number on EUR-Lex before use. In L01 check whether the identifier rule belongs to Art. 12 and the definition to Art. 2; do not cite 'Art. 2(30)' as the identifier rule until read.

checked.claim: data.context partly covers NGSI-LD context signalling (allowlist), and the header-versus-body rule is not covered.
checked.evidence: capabilities.md: data.context checks context references against a pinned allowlist and fetches no context. It does not read Link headers.

checked.claim: A changed or unreachable @context URL is detectable by fetching the context twice and by data.context.
checked.evidence: data.context fetches no context, so it cannot detect drift or unreachability; it checks only listed URLs against an allowlist. The 'fetch twice' step has no engine check and would need a new capability.
checked.correction: Say data.context catches only a context URL outside the allowlist; context drift needs a new pinned-content check (hash of the context file) and a network-capable fetch.

checked.claim: The capability behind access.restricted_fields is access.restricted_fields.
checked.evidence: The check access.restricted_fields runs on the capability access.policy, and the policy channels are fetch, search, export, error, HTML. A subscription notification channel (failure_modes[7]) is not among them.
checked.correction: Write existing_capability as access.policy and state that notification payloads are not a covered channel; a new channel or adapter is needed.

checked.claim: integrity.jws supported, integrity.cose interface_only, identifier.parse limited to GS1 form, persistence.versions written for passport version URLs, aas.validate covers AAS side only.
checked.evidence: States match the manifest: integrity.jws supported, integrity.cose interface_only, persistence.versions experimental, aas.validate experimental and not a complete DPP statement. identifier.consistency compares exact text of the carrier id with the resolved passport id.

checked.evidence: The URL appears in a search result for this session, but I did not open the paper; the licence and the absence claim were not re-checked.

rule5_findings.problem: Calls EN 18223 a 'CEN/CENELEC DPP data model' and says OPC 30450-1 maps it. This characterises the content of a protected EN, relayed from a third-party listing, and the catalogue title of EN 18223 is 'Digital Product Passport - System interoperability'.
rule5_findings.fix: Write: 'The OPC listing names EN 18223:2026 (title: Digital Product Passport - System interoperability, CEN/CLC/JTC 24) as its input. The EN content was not read.' Drop 'data model' as a description of the EN.

rule5_findings.problem: Repeats the OPC description that the EN defines a data model that is mapped to ObjectTypes. That is a statement about EN content from a secondary source.
rule5_findings.fix: Say only that the listing names EN 18223:2026 as a normative input; tag the statement secondary_only.

rule5_findings.problem: Describes the EN 18223 mapping as something 'the engine team must not read'. This is acceptable as a fence note, but it implies content ('mapping') of the EN.
rule5_findings.fix: Reword to: 'The listing names EN 18223:2026; the engine team does not read it.'

missed_items.fact: Secondary sources place unique identifiers in Article 12 of Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 and describe Article 10 as the DPP requirements article. The target file uses Art. 2(30) and Art. 10(1) for identifier and carrier rules and never cites Art. 12. Needs EUR-Lex reading.

Secondary catalogue listings show EN 18223:2026 titled 'Digital Product Passport - System interoperability', handled by CEN/CLC/JTC 24/WG 4; one listing gives publication on 2026-05-27. The target file records no publication date.

In WoT Discovery only the /things listing is required; create, read, update, delete, /events and the three /search endpoints are optional. A black-box test must probe for support before it expects them.

missed_items.topic: NGSI-LD error type for duplicate create
missed_items.fact: The ETSI spec defines the error type https://uri.etsi.org/ngsi-ld/errors/AlreadyExists, which gives the oracle for the failure mode 'POST of an existing id'.

missed_items.topic: Battery data model for a DPP on these stacks
missed_items.fact: An open Battery Pass data model repository exists and could serve as the application profile that the file says is missing; whether it has an NGSI-LD form was not verified.

overall: The file is largely reliable on what I could re-check. All nine repository metadata blocks match gh api output (push dates for fast-moving repos have already moved), all 20 DOIs match Crossref, and the NGSI-LD, WoT Discovery, DTDL and OPC 30450-1 mechanisms and listing facts match the primary sources. The weak points are the ESPR article numbers, which stay unverified and may omit Art. 12 on unique identifiers, and three engine mappings: data.context cannot detect context drift because it fetches nothing, the access check runs on access.policy, and notification payloads are not a policy channel. Rule 5 exposure is small but real: the file describes EN 18223 as a data model on the word of a third-party listing. I did not re-read the paper abstracts or the CEUR paper.
